correctness.rationale: For the canonical right-continuous half-line BV representative, integration against Df reduces the quotient exactly to unit steps. A step in ((j−1)/n,j/n] uses the negative-binomial survival at j, equivalently the CDF of Y=Gamma(j)/Gamma(n) with independent factors. Integrating this CDF by parts gives J (the truncated first moment is j/(n−1) times the shifted beta CDF). The integrated response has second derivative 2 times the positive density, so only the two formal cell ends matter; a jump beyond 1 has a smaller sampled tail than the jump at 1. For s≤1, the response is E|Y−s|−E(Y−1)+, where the last expression denotes the expectation of the positive part. With a=j/n bounded away from zero the centered exponential sum W=(U−aV)/sqrt(n) has variance a(1+a) and uniform Wasserstein normal error O(n^−1/2); Cauchy–Schwarz with E(n/V−1)^2=O(1/n) controls multiplying W by n/V. Thus E|Y−s|=sqrt(2 a(1+a)/(pi n))+O(1/n) at either endpoint. When a→0 the exact inverse-gamma second moments give o(n^−1/2). For the nonstandard tail step, the density has Stirling exponent −nD_a(y) with D_a(y)=(1+a)log((1+y)/(1+a))−a log(y/a), D'_a(y)=(y−a)/(y(1+y)); on a fixed multiple of sqrt(log n/n) near a≈1 Taylor expansion gives a uniform relative 1+o(1) Gaussian density. Chernoff applied to U−yV at lambda=(y−a)/(y(1+a)) gives P(Y≥y)≤exp(−nD_a(y)); Cauchy–Schwarz with bounded second moments then makes the contribution outside a sufficiently wide window negligible. At a=1−c sqrt(log n/n)+O(1/n), the Gaussian excess integral is asymptotic to 2 n^(−1/2−c²/4)/(c² sqrt(pi) log n). The competitor c=sqrt(2) gives the sharp leading limit and a full-moment loss of (3/(2 sqrt(pi)))sqrt(2 log n)/n+O(1/n). Any maximizing sequence must have a→1. Larger fixed c incurs a strictly larger full-moment loss by monotonicity of the variance profile; smaller fixed positive c incurs, by stochastic ordering in j, a tail dominating sqrt(log n)/n. This proves the location limit for every winning pair, unchanged by the 1/n endpoint choice.
